title: Fix/modernize the socketio examples
body:
The socketio examples are difficult to get to run because some have not been updated, and in general they have dangling configuration so they won't work out of the box, meaning we also don't test which again makes them liable to break.  Also some were still written with pre-genericfileio.

Closes: #1712 

This MR updates as many as possible:
 * Use modern syntax (`calc.socketio(...)`) where possible, so ASE takes care of most of the boilerplate
 * Rely on the configuration file.

# Checklist: `x` (done) or `~` (irrelevant)

- [ ] [I am familiar with **ASE's contribution guidelines.**](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/development/contribute.html)
- [ ] [**Doc strings** in code changed in this MR are up to date.](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/development/python_codingstandard.html#writing-documentation-in-the-code)
- [ ] [**Unit tests** have been added for new or changed code.](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/development/tests.html)
- [ ] [**Changes** have been added in `changelog.d` using `scriv`.](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/development/writing_changelog.html)
- [ ] [**Issue is resolved** via "closes #XXXX" if applicable.](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/project/issues/managing_issues.html#closing-issues-automatically)
author: askhl

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
The genericfileio calculators have better control over how the calculator command is handled, which allows them to do the Right Thing automatically `.socketio()`.  That simplifies many examples so users no longer have to ensure that socketio options and calculator options are consistent.

The examples now rely on the configuration file in order to require minimal configuration (some of them still need specific pseudopotential files though).

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: I'll take the liberty of merging.
